metadata.title: Markers Gone Does Not Mean Merged Right
metadata.note: Week 8 how-to video. Voice hai/Bella for @HumanitariansAI. Content only from the table-building chat; no claim about when the conflict happened or how it ended.
metadata.author: Risa Samanta

beats.narration_text: A merge conflict looks like an error, but it is just two edits to the same line. This is Risa Samanta's how-to video for the week: reading a merge conflict, and checking the file after you resolve it.

props.command: claude "why am I getting this conflict?"
output: keep the right parts of each

beats.narration_text: Here is what happened. My branch, visual edits, inserted a new table directly above a heading. The development branch had fixed the garbled characters in that very heading. Git could not tell which version of the line to keep, so it marked both. The other table, twenty-three point four point two, merged cleanly, because it did not sit next to a changed line.
beats.visual_intent: Real drifted caption names from the actual repo animating toward a clean sectioned scheme. Show the mechanism, not a count.

props.caption: Git cannot choose, so it marks both

beats.narration_text: In the file, a conflict is three marker lines around the two versions: my side, with the table and the garbled heading, a line of equals signs, then development's clean heading. The fix is to keep the table and the clean heading, and delete the garbled heading and the three marker lines.

props.title: the conflict, in outline
props.code:
<<<<<<< visual-edits
(the table block)
**Concentration Ã— Time (CÃ—T) Pharmacodynamics**
=======
**Concentration × Time (C×T) Pharmacodynamics**
>>>>>>> development

# keep: the table + the clean heading
# delete: the garbled heading + the three marker lines
props.sparkLine: Keep both parts, drop the markers.

beats.narration_text: Resolving is not the same as being right. After I resolved it, I had Claude check the file. The conflict markers were gone and both tables sat in the right places, but the garbled heading had survived, and so had the old wording from before development's fixes. Committing it would have overwritten development's text changes and brought the garbled characters back.

props.command: claude "check my resolved file: are the markers gone, and does it still have development's changes?"

beats.narration_text: Three searches catch it. Search for the marker lines. Search for the garbled characters. And search for a phrase that only the development branch has, in this case a chlorambucil volume of distribution of point three, to prove the file really contains development's text. If that phrase is missing, you kept the wrong side.

props.title: checks after resolving
props.code:
1. search for   <<<<<<<   =======   >>>>>>>
2. search for   Ã   â€        (garbled characters)
3. search for a phrase only development has:
     chlorambucil, Vd ~0.3

# phrase missing = you kept the wrong side
props.sparkLine: Prove the other branch is in the file.

beats.narration_text: The fix was to abort the merge and merge again, keeping both parts this time. To avoid it next time, pull development into your branch before you insert tables, so you start from the corrected text.

props.command: claude "what is the safest way to redo this merge?"

beats.narration_text: Your turn. When you resolve a conflict, ask Claude to check the file afterward: markers gone, garbled characters gone, and a phrase from the other branch present. Then commit, not before.

props.command: claude "check my resolved file: no markers, no garbled characters, and this phrase from the other branch is present"

beats.narration_text: Markers gone does not mean merged right. This has been Risa Samanta's how-to, voiced by Bella for Humanitarians AI. Check the file, then commit.

props.title: Markers Gone Does Not Mean Merged Right.
